messages.subject: Error message: Error in as.environment(where) : 'where' is missing
parts:
Sorry, but I can't figure this message out. I'm trying to get a series
of stacked bar charts across the page. Here is a part of my data:

all.ratings <- structure(list(comp.name = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L,
3L, 3L, 3L, 3L), .Label = c("Class mgmt", "Comm with students",
"Engaging Students", "Flexible, responsive", "Learning culture",
"Physical space", "Respectful env", "Student behav", "Using assessments",
"Using questions"), class = "factor"), Freq = c(0.0383631713554987,
0.59079283887468, 0.370843989769821, 0.0101522842639594, 0.408629441624365,
0.581218274111675, 0.00255102040816327, 0.0408163265306122, 0.642857142857143,
0.313775510204082), Rating = structure(c(2L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 3L,
4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L), .Label = c("1", "2", "3", "4"), class = c("ordered",
"factor"))), .Names = c("comp.name", "Freq", "Rating"), row.names = c(NA,
10L), class = "data.frame")

Using this code:

ggplot(all.ratings, aes(y=Freq, fill=Rating)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") +
facet_grid(. ~ comp.name )

This is giving the error in the subject line. Can anyone tell me what I'm doing wrong?

TIA.
--
Stuart Luppescu <s...@ccsr.uchicago.edu>
University of Chicago

messages.subject: Re: Error message: Error in as.environment(where) : 'where' is missing
parts:
No, agreed, it's not a very helpful error message. The basic problem
is that geom_bar requires an 'x' aesthetic and you haven't defined
one. How about doing this:

ggplot(all.ratings, aes(x=comp.name,y=Freq, fill=Rating)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity")

Ben

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Error message: Error in as.environment(where) : 'where' is missing
parts:
Hi Stuart:

If you want to keep the faceting intact, here's an alternative
approach with a few extra bells and whistles:

ggplot( all.ratings, aes(x = 1, y = Freq, fill = Rating) ) +
geom_bar( stat = "identity", position = "stack" ) +
theme_bw() +
facet_wrap( ~ comp.name, nrow = 1 ) +
labs( x = NULL, y = "Proportion" ) +
scale_fill_manual( values = c("black", "orange", "blue", "violet") ) +
theme( panel.grid = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_blank(),
axis.ticks.x = theme_blank() )

The problem with using 1 as a 'variable' (especially as numeric rather
than factor) is that it adds a numeric x-scale to each bar by default,
so the added theme() code gets rid of it and (for this purpose) the
unnecessary grid lines.

Dennis
